To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) microbial physiology is controlled and regulated by the concentrations of metabolites, and that (2) the thermodynamics of microbial metabolism is determined by the free energy change of the overall reaction, not by the free energy changes of the component reactions.

the thermodynamic efficiency of microbial growth is not a fixed property of the organism, that the efficiency of growth can vary over a wide range of values, that the efficiency depends on the composition of the growth medium and that the efficiency of microbial growth can be predicted from the composition of the medium.
the thermodynamic and kinetic control of microbial metabolism is a function of the concentrations of metabolites in the cell and that these concentrations are controlled by the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel mathematical methods for analyzing and modeling microbial growth, and the application of these methods in the context of microbial physiology and biotechnology.
the quantitative aspects of metabolic regulation and control, the thermodynamics of metabolic reactions, and the development of mathematical models of microbial metabolism.
the quantitative analysis of metabolic control and regulation, the thermodynamics of microbial metabolism and the development and application of novel methods of metabolic control analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no longer any need to choose between reductionistic and holistic views of microbial physiology and metabolism, because the new concepts allow us to integrate them.
the new approaches have led to a better understanding of microbial metabolism and energetics, and that the new approaches should be considered as a valuable addition to the traditional ones.

the new methods of control analysis are not only a powerful and versatile tool for the analysis of microbial physiology and bioenergetics but they also serve to remove part or the discordance between holism and reductionism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamic approach to microbial physiology has reached a level of maturity that allows it to be used in a predictive way.
the thermodynamic analysis of the control of metabolism is now possible and is a useful tool for understanding microbial physiology.

we have been able to show that the control and regulation exerted by metabolic enzymes can be quantitatively described in terms of the thermodynamic properties of the enzymes and their substrates and products, and the properties of the cellular environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the new approaches are powerful and elegant, they are not a panacea for understanding the control of microbial metabolism.
there is a need to re-evaluate our understanding of microbial physiology, in the context of the new concepts.

, in principle, the quantitative analysis of the control, regulation, and thermodynamics of metabolism should be based on a combination of three types of information: the stoichiometry of the reactions of interest; their kinetic parameters; and the thermodynamic properties of their reactants.
